ov: Armoured crustaceans with the tail tucked under the body, able to run sideways. The crab shape has evolved several separate times, a process called carcinisation, so crabs aren’t one natural group.

why.p: Mostly hermit crabs, which are commonly kept as pets and can live for 30 years.
why.et: Crabs make up about 20% of the sea crustaceans caught or farmed for food.

len: A few mm (pea crab) to a 4 m leg span (Japanese spider crab)
rg: Oceans worldwide, and a substantial number of species live in fresh water or on land.
df: Many are marine omnivores eating algae, molluscs, worms and other crustaceans; others are specialist plant- or meat-eaters.
fx: Crabs make up about 20% of the sea crustaceans caught or farmed for food.

_cf.tip: Unlike most crabs, a hermit crab has a soft abdomen that it protects in a borrowed shell.
Despite its name it is not a crab or even a crustacean: it is a chelicerate, more closely related to spiders, ticks and scorpions.
